newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-LEONHARDSEN MAINTAINS NORWAY'S WINNING RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEONHARDSEN MAINTAINS NORWAY'S WINNING RECORD.

text.p: Midfielder Oyvind Leonhardsen extended Norway's 100 percent record in their World Cup qualifying campaign with the decisive goal as they beat Switzerland 1-0 on Sunday.
Leonhardsen's strike after 32 minutes was enough to keep Norway top of European group three with three victories in as many matches.
The Swiss, now third in the group and six points off the pace, initially contained the Norwegian attack which had hit eight goals in the two previous games.
However, Norway broke through when Tore Andre Flo unleashed a blistering drive from just inside the penalty area that forced goalkeeper Marco Pascolo to make a diving save.
Leonhardsen, who plays for English premier league Wimbledon, pounced on the rebound and hammered it into the empty net, silencing Swiss fans in a sell-out crowd of 22,000.
The goal prompted an immediate Swiss offensive as they tried to get back on terms before halftime.

Switzerland continued to press in the second half but Norway's defence, which has yet to concede a goal in their three qualifiers, continued to frustrate the home attack, particularly Stephane Chapuisat.
Twice goalkeeper Frode Grodas denied the tricky Borussia Dortmund striker when he looked sure to score.
Just seven minutes into the second half, Grodas charged off his line to make a sprawling save from Chapuisat, then denied him again from point-blank range in the 78th minute.

Switzerland: 1-Marco Pascolo, 2-Raphael Wicky, 3-Marco Walker, 4-Stephane Henchoz, 5-Ramon Vega, 6-Murat Yakin (Blaise Piffaretti 88th), 7-Johann Vogel, 8-Massimo Lombardo (Nestor Subiat 70th), 9-Kubilay Turkyilmaz, 10-Ciriaco Sforza, 11-Stephane Chapuisat (Christophe Bonvin 85th).

Norway: 1-Frode Grodas, 2-Alf-Inge Haland, 3-Ronny Johnsen, 4-Henning Berg, 5-Roger Nilsen, 6-Tore Andre Flo (Ole Gunnar Solskjaer 73rd), 7-Erik Mykland (Stale Solbakken 53rd), 8-Oyvind Leonhardsen, 9-Frank Strandli, 10-Kjetil Rekdal, 11-Egil Ostenstad (Havard Flo 87th).
